sun.upright:
Aries likes to be first through the door, and a Page of Swords drawn for your light gives you a reason to go through it asking questions. Aries is cardinal fire, ruled by Mars, the sign of starting things. The Page is air, and fire and air are friendly elements, so there's no drag here at all. An idea turns up and it catches straight away. You've got an opinion on it before lunch and a plan by the evening.

From the inside it's a kind of itch. You want to find out, argue it through, test it on someone. The Emperor is the Major that belongs to Aries, the ruler who already knows how things should be run, and the Page is about as far from him as a court card gets, the junior of the suit, ready to learn. For an Aries Sun that's a funny position to be in, because you'd normally prefer to be the one with the answers. It's good for you, though. Asking is its own way of going first, and you're very good at it once you stop worrying about looking green.

At work it's the new area you want to get into, where you'd be the least experienced person in the room, and it suits you better than you'd expect. In an argument with a friend or a sibling it's the sharp point you've spotted that nobody else has, and you'll want to make it immediately. Make it, by all means. Ask one real question first, one you don't already know the answer to, and listen to what comes back.
sun.reversed:
An Aries Sun with the Page upside down can end up picking fights just to feel awake. The quick mind gets bored and goes looking for an opponent, a colleague who's wrong about something small, a partner who used the wrong word. Mars rules Aries, and with the card reversed the air fans the temper instead of the curiosity. You start five things, argue about all of them and finish none.

It shows at work as the email fired off before you'd read the whole thread, and at home as a debate about something neither of you cares about. Before you hit send on anything sharp, read the other person's message again from the top. Half the time, the thing you were about to argue with isn't in it.

moon.upright:
Feelings move fast in an Aries Moon. Something annoys you, you flare, you say so, and then it's gone, and you're a bit baffled when other people are still upset an hour later. Your Moon is in cardinal fire, a sign Mars rules, and it's soothed by doing something. This Page brings air into that, and air and fire help each other along, so whatever you're feeling turns into words very quickly.

That's handy, mostly. You can name what's bothering you, which a lot of people can't. The catch is that the words come out at the speed of the feeling, with the edges still on. You might notice you're spikier than usual, or that you want to talk something through straight away and the other person needs a day. Some of what's going on is plain restlessness. The mind's woken up and it wants something to chew on, and if it doesn't get a proper problem it'll find a small one.

Your body will probably tell you about it first. There's a jittery, wound-up energy that doesn't settle well in the evening, and sleep can come late. At home, it can look like picking at a housemate or partner over something that doesn't really matter. Give the energy somewhere to go. A hard walk or a run before the conversation you want to have will make it a better conversation.
moon.reversed:
When the Page turns over on an Aries Moon, hurt comes out as a sharp line. You don't say you were upset. You say something clever and cutting, and then you feel worse. Mars rules the sign your Moon sits in, and Mars would always prefer to attack than feel exposed, so this reversed air card hands it the words to do it with. The people closest to you get the sharpest of it, usually over nothing much.

It can also be a head that won't switch off, replaying an argument and writing better comebacks at one in the morning. That shows in your sleep, and in the texts you send late at night. Put the phone out of reach after ten. If the comeback still seems worth saying when you wake up, say it then, and say it more kindly.

rising.upright:
Strangers usually meet Aries rising at speed. You come in direct, a bit restless, ready to get on with it, and with Mars ruling the chart there's a sense that you've already decided something. Drawing the Page of Swords for your mask adds a sharp, questioning look to that. Air and fire get on easily, so it doesn't slow you down at all. If anything it gives the forward push a point.

People see someone alert and a little combative, who asks the direct question in the first five minutes. In the Rider-Waite picture the young figure stands on a rise with the sword up and the head turned, as if something caught their ear, and that's quite close to how you're coming across. Some people love it, especially the ones who are tired of small talk. Others feel slightly cross-examined and you may not notice, because to you it was just curiosity. Aries rising starts things by reacting, and air makes the reaction verbal.

In a job interview it can win you the job, since you'll be the candidate who asked something interesting. In a new team, or meeting a partner's friends, it can come across as a bit much. Let the other person finish their sentence before you come in with the question. It's still a good question a few seconds later.
rising.reversed:
Aries rising with this Page reversed can walk into a room already arguing. You interrupt, correct someone's facts, make a joke at a stranger's expense and wonder why the room's gone cool. Mars runs your chart, and the upside-down air card makes that first impulse come out as words that sting. Usually it's nerves, and you'd hate to be told so.

It turns up at work in meetings, where you jump in with the objection before the idea's been explained, and on first dates, which can end up feeling like a debate. It turns up online too. Pick one setting, the next meeting perhaps, and make your first contribution a question you actually want answered. People will read you quite differently, and you'll hear more of what they think.

sun.upright:
A Taurus Sun believes what it can hold. Taurus is fixed earth, ruled by Venus, and you build yourself slowly out of things that have proved they last, the job you know, the money in the account, the people who turned up. The Page of Swords arrives full of questions and new information, and air and earth are opposed elements. One lives in ideas and the other wants evidence. So this is a slightly uncomfortable draw for you, and a useful one.

What you'll probably notice is that something you took as settled is being questioned, and some of the questioning is coming from you. The Hierophant is Taurus's own Major, the card of tradition and the way things have always been done, and the Page is the young one at the back of the class asking why. You don't like being hurried into a new opinion. You don't have to be. Fixed earth changes its mind slowly, and when it does change, it tends to stay changed, which makes you a better learner than people assume.

With money, it might be the contract or the super or the mortgage you've never read properly. At work, it could be a skill you've avoided because it looked fiddly or faddish. Pick one of them and learn it properly, at your own pace, until you could explain it to someone else.
sun.reversed:
Taurus can dig its heels in over an idea as firmly as over anything else, and with a Taurus Sun and the Page reversed that's often what's going on. New information turns up and you refuse to look at it. Or the opposite happens and you're reading everything, every article about the market, every opinion on the thing you've been meaning to decide, and none of it gets you closer to acting. Air and earth pull against each other anyway, and in the reversal they stop talking altogether.

Money shows it first, a decision you've researched to death or one you've refused to research at all. At work it can look like quiet stubbornness when something changes. Choose the one fact you'd need to know to move, find it out, and then make the call within a few days.

moon.upright:
The body settles a Taurus Moon. Good food, a warm bed, the same walk at the same time, someone familiar in the next room. Your Moon is in fixed earth, ruled by Venus, and what you need is steadiness you can feel. This Page belongs to air, the element set against earth, and it brings the one thing a Taurus Moon finds hardest to digest, a busy head.

It can feel like having a radio on in another room that you can't find to turn off. Thoughts turn up uninvited, a worry about money, a conversation you're still going over, something you read that unsettled you. Earth deals with things by sitting with them until they settle, and air keeps stirring them up again. The good side is that some of those questions are worth asking. Taurus Moons can put up with an uncomfortable situation for a very long time, and the Page is poking at one of them.

Sleep is where you'll feel it, lying there with the list going round. It also shows at meals, eating while scrolling and not tasting anything. Do something with your hands when the thinking gets loud, bake, dig, fold the washing, and let the question sit in the back of your mind while you do. It'll often have an answer by the time you've finished.
moon.reversed:
Worry tends to go into the body with a Taurus Moon, and with this card reversed it's been going in for a while. Your jaw's tight, your shoulders are up, and you're telling everyone you're fine. The Page upside down is a mind that's anxious and can't say about what, so it lands on small things, the bill, the noise next door, a tone in someone's message. Fixed earth holds on to all of it, and it builds up quietly.

The other version is stubborn silence, refusing to hear a piece of news because it would mean changing something. Home and sleep show it, and so does your appetite. Get outside and walk somewhere green without your phone. When you come back, say out loud to one person what's actually bothering you, even if it's only half worked out.

rising.upright:
Look at the Page's feet in the Rider-Waite picture, planted on rough, uneven ground while the wind throws the clouds about. Taurus rising knows how to stand still. You tend to come across as calm, unhurried and pleasant, with Venus ruling the chart, the kind of person strangers assume won't make a fuss. The Page puts a sharper look on that easy face. Air and earth are opposites in temperament, so it doesn't blend in quietly, and people notice.

They see someone who's paying close attention and who might ask an awkward question. You're less willing to go along with things just because it's easier. In a meeting you might want to know where the numbers came from. In a shop you might ask what the thing's actually made of. It's a slightly odd feeling for Taurus rising, because your usual way of starting something is slow and steady, and here your first move is to check. There's nothing wrong with that. You're harder to sell to, and that's no bad thing.

At work, colleagues may start to see you as someone with judgement, not just someone reliable. In a negotiation or when buying something big, the questions will save you money. Keep asking them, politely, until you've heard an answer that makes sense to you.
rising.reversed:
With Taurus rising, a reversed Page can make you look closed and suspicious. You stand at the edge, arms folded, visibly not believing a word, and people pick it up before you've spoken. Venus rules your chart and usually softens how you come across. With the card turned over, the pull between air and earth shows on your face instead. You've decided something's off and you're not saying what.

It turns up with salespeople and new colleagues, and at gatherings where you only half know people. It can also swing into nosiness, asking personal questions too early. If you're doubtful about something, say so once, calmly, and ask the question. It'll make you seem far less forbidding than the folded arms do.

sun.upright:
Gemini is inside this card's own territory. The Page of Swords gathers up air at its youngest, drawn from Gemini, Libra and Aquarius together, and your Sun is in mutable air, ruled by Mercury, the planet of messages and quick thinking. So the card is speaking your language. It turns up everything you're good at, the curiosity, the wit, the ability to pick up anything in an afternoon, and it turns up the scatter as well.

What you're building in yourself is a mind people can rely on, and the difficulty is depth. You probably have ten tabs open, three side projects, a book half-read on the bedside table and another in your bag. Each of them is interesting. The Lovers is the Major for Gemini, and that card is about choosing one thing and meaning it, which is the part the Page hasn't learnt yet. Mutable air can go anywhere, and some days it goes everywhere. You'll know the feeling, the buzz of starting and then the slight flatness when you look back and nothing's finished.

At work this is a great card for research, writing, anything that needs someone to find out fast. With a brother or sister, or an old friend, it can mean conversations that go on for hours. Pick the one project you'd most like to have finished, and give it the next three evenings, all of them.
sun.reversed:
Cleverness can turn into a place to hide, and a Gemini Sun with this card reversed is often hiding in it. You've got a quick answer for everything, a joke for anything serious, and a habit of changing the subject just before it gets personal. Air on air, upside down, tends to mean lots of talk and very little landing. Gossip is part of it too. It's fun, it's easy, and it isn't quite kind.

You'll spot it in group chats and at work, where you've half-promised four people four things. Friends might have stopped telling you secrets, and you may have noticed without asking why. Go quiet in the chat for a day or two. Then finish one of the half-promised things and tell the person it's done.

moon.upright:
Talking settles a Gemini Moon, and so does knowing things. You feel safe when you've got the information, and you tend to work through a feeling by describing it to someone, often at length. Your Moon is in mutable air, ruled by Mercury, and the Page is air too, with Gemini one of the three signs it's made from, so the card doubles what's already there. The mind that soothes you is suddenly running quite fast.

That can feel lovely, a buzzy, alert, interested stretch where everything's worth a conversation. It can also tip into nerves without much warning. Air amplified has nowhere to put itself down, and a Gemini Moon can go from curious to anxious in the space of one bad news story. You might notice your breathing is high in your chest, or that you keep picking up your phone without knowing what you're looking for. The need underneath is simple. You want to feel you know what's going on, and the Page keeps showing you there's more to find out.

Sleep is the first thing to look after, since your head will want to keep working late. With friends, it's the one who'll let you talk it through, and the one who'll stop you. Take a long walk with no headphones in and let your thoughts run out of steam on their own.
moon.reversed:
A Gemini Moon with the Page upside down tends to feed its worries information. You look it up, then look up something else, then read the comments. A rumour or a half-heard remark gets into your head and goes round and round. The doubled air has no weight on it, so nothing settles, and you can feel wired and flat at the same time.

It shows in your sleep and in your phone, and in how often you're repeating the same story to different friends. Some of them have heard it three times. Choose one trustworthy person, tell them the whole thing once, and then agree with yourself to stop checking for a couple of days. The facts will still be there when you look again.

rising.upright:
Gemini rising tends to open with a question. You're quick, friendly, a bit restless, and strangers often find you easy to talk to within a minute. Mercury rules your chart, so how you start anything is by noticing and chatting. This Page is air as well, from the same airy family as your rising sign, and it sharpens the whole performance. The questions get pointed. The wit gets a bit of an edge.

People will find you interesting, and some of them will find you slightly too much. You might catch yourself asking something a little personal, or saying the thing everyone else was thinking, and watching the room react. Gemini rising is used to being the lively one, and this is lively with a blade in its hand. It's usually fun. It does mean you're being read as sharper and more opinionated than you feel inside, which can surprise you.

At a party or a networking do, you'll be remembered. In a new job, you'll find out how things really work faster than anyone. On a first date, the banter will be good. Keep one question back for the second time you meet someone, so there's something left to find out.
rising.reversed:
Gemini rising reversed can come across as slippery. You say something different to each person, you're charming and then gone, and people aren't sure which version is you. With this card upside down, the Mercury side of your chart goes into sarcasm or chatter, and the quick mind uses words to keep people at a distance. It isn't that you're dishonest. You're nervous, and talking is what you do with nerves.

It shows at work in rumours you pass on without checking, and socially in the flaky text that cancels at the last minute. Online it's the witty reply that turns out to be unkind. Before you repeat something about someone, ask yourself whether you'd say it with them in the room. If you wouldn't, leave it.

sun.upright:
Cancer is cardinal water, ruled by the Moon, and a Cancer Sun builds itself around the people it looks after. You want to protect, to make a home, to be the one who remembers everyone's birthday. Swords are air, and air and water are neutral to each other. They don't fight. They also don't understand each other without some effort, so this card asks you to introduce your head to your heart.

Usually what that means is a question you've been avoiding, often a family one. Why a parent did what they did. What really happened with the money after a grandparent died. Whether a friendship that's felt one-sided for a while actually is one-sided. The Chariot is Cancer's Major, a figure in armour driving forward, and Cancer Suns tend to keep that armour on around hard facts. The Page takes it off for a moment. It wants to know, and it's brave about it, in a slightly clumsy, young way. You may find the facts are easier to live with than the not knowing.

At home it might be a conversation at the kitchen table you've been putting off. At work it might be speaking up about something unfair to a colleague, which Cancer does well once it's decided to. Write your question down, in one sentence, and then ask it.
sun.reversed:
Words become a shell for a Cancer Sun with this card reversed. Something hurt you, and instead of saying so you've gone sarcastic, or you've started gathering evidence about who said what. The Moon rules Cancer, and the reversed Page gives that moody tide a sharp tongue. You're defending yourself before anyone has attacked.

Family is the usual place, especially a sibling or parent who knows exactly which button to press. It can also show as passing on something told to you in confidence, because it felt good to be the one who knew. Say the hurt thing plainly to the person who caused it, without the clever remark on the end. Then leave it for a day and see what they do.

moon.upright:
The Moon rules Cancer, so a Cancer Moon is the Moon in its own sign and your feelings run the show most of the time. You need safety, the right people close, home the way you like it. The Page of Swords walks into that with a notebook. It's an air card, and air has no natural rapport with water, so it wants to understand what you feel, which for a Cancer Moon is a strange idea. Usually you just feel it.

What you might notice is that you're thinking about your moods, watching yourself be upset and wondering why. That can be useful. Cardinal water acts on feelings quickly, and sometimes the Page's pause is the thing that stops you ringing someone in a state. It can also be unsettling, a bit like hearing your own voice on a recording. There might be a comment someone made that you keep turning over, trying to work out what they meant. Sharp words land hard on a Cancer Moon, and this is a card of sharp words, so you're probably touchier about tone than usual.

Home is where it'll show, in how you talk with the people you live with. Sleep too, with the day's conversations running round. When something's said that stings, ask what they meant by it, calmly, before you decide.
moon.reversed:
With a Cancer Moon, a reversed Page can mean reading far too much into things. A short text becomes a sign they're angry. A pause on the phone becomes proof. Your Moon is in the sign it rules, so feelings are always loud, and with this card upside down they get a busy, suspicious mind attached, going over every word for a hidden meaning.

It shows at home and in family relationships, and sometimes as eavesdropping or checking up on people. Sleep goes, too, usually around three in the morning. Before you act on what you think someone meant, ask them. Keep it short, say what you heard and how it landed, and give them a chance to tell you what they intended.

rising.upright:
People tend to meet Cancer rising and feel looked after. You're warm but careful, and there's often a slight shell until you've worked out whether someone's safe. The Moon rules your chart, and it makes your first move a feeling one. Put the Page of Swords over that and the careful part comes forward. Air doesn't clash with water, and people will see someone more watchful and more inquisitive than usual.

You ask questions, lots of them, some of them sharp. You notice who's being evasive. You might not bother smoothing things over for a stranger, because you'd like to find out what's actually going on. For cardinal water, which usually starts things by caring, that's a different way in, and it can feel a bit exposing. You're using your head where you'd normally use your instinct. People may find you more direct, and some of them will respect it.

It's useful in a new job, meeting a partner's family, or any situation where you need to know the lie of the land before you settle. It can put a date slightly on the back foot. Ask your questions, and let a bit of the warmth show while you do, so people don't feel they're being assessed.
rising.reversed:
The claws come out first with Cancer rising and this Page reversed. You meet someone new and within a few minutes you've made a sharp little remark, or gone quiet and suspicious, sizing them up. The Moon rules your chart, and when you're unsure of a place you defend it with words. People can read that as unfriendliness when it's actually nerves.

It shows up in new workplaces, at a partner's family gatherings, and online, where it's easy to get prickly with strangers. Sometimes it's quieter, a guarded vagueness when someone asks you a simple question. Give people one straight, friendly answer early on. You can keep the rest of yourself back until you're ready.

sun.upright:
Leo Suns are usually the ones telling the story at dinner, and with the Page of Swords on your light the story's got sharper lines in it. Leo is fixed fire, the only sign the Sun rules, and you want to be seen doing something that matters, with some warmth coming back your way. The Page is air. Fire and air are on good terms, each feeding the other, so the card adds wit and speed to a Sun that already likes an audience.

The tension is about rank. Strength is Leo's Major, the steady, grown-up kind of confidence, and the Page is the most junior figure in the whole suit of Swords, a beginner with a lot to prove. Leo doesn't love being the beginner. I've seen plenty of Leo Suns avoid learning something new in public because they couldn't stand being bad at it for a month. The Page doesn't care how it looks. It's too interested. If you can borrow some of that, you'll pick up a skill quickly, and you'll probably end up teaching it, which is the part Leo enjoys.

In creative work it's the writing class, the improv night, the pitch where you get grilled and hold your own. With children, your own or anyone's, it's answering their endless questions properly. Book the thing where you'll be the least polished person in the room, and go twice before you decide whether you like it.
sun.reversed:
Pride and a quick tongue make a hard pair, and that's usually the trouble with a reversed Page on a Leo Sun. Someone questions your work, or laughs at the wrong moment, and the comeback's out before you've thought. It's funny, and it's meant to hurt. Fixed fire holds on to a slight, and the air here gives it words to keep throwing.

Sometimes it goes the other way and you won't try anything you might look silly doing, so you talk about the novel you'll write and never open the file. Work and romance both feel it, the colleague you've decided is your rival, the partner who teased you once too often. Leo is usually generous once it's been heard. Say the thing that actually stung, plainly, and leave the wit out of it.

moon.upright:
Warmth is what a Leo Moon runs on. You need to feel loved out loud, noticed, a bit special, and when you get that you're the most generous person in the room. Your Moon is in fixed fire, ruled by the Sun. The Page brings air, and air feeds fire, so your feelings get quick and articulate, and you may find you want to talk about what you feel far more than usual, preferably to someone who's listening properly.

There's a sharper side too. The Page is a card of honest words, and a Leo Moon can be very hurt by honesty that arrives without warmth. A friend's offhand remark about your cooking, or a partner correcting a story you're telling, can sit with you all evening. Fixed fire doesn't let things go quickly. You're not being silly. Your feelings are tied to being appreciated, and this card says what it sees, which isn't always flattering. It can also be you doing the saying, and discovering you've got a talent for the witty, loving tease.

With a partner, this is good for the kind of conversation where you both say what you want. With friends, you'll notice who's quick to praise you and who's quick to correct you. When something stings, tell the person the same day. Leo Moons feel better fast once it's out.
moon.reversed:
A Leo Moon with this Page reversed can turn a small hurt into a performance. You weren't thanked, or someone got the credit you wanted, and by the evening you're giving a speech about it, or you've gone grandly silent and are waiting for someone to ask. The air fans the fire here, so the feeling spreads quickly, and the words come out bigger than the hurt.

The people who get it are usually the closest, a partner or a parent. It can also come out as sarcasm towards someone you secretly admire. Leo Moons are loyal, and they expect the same back, sometimes without saying so. Check whether you're tired or hungry before you decide you've been wronged. Then tell the person in two sentences what you'd have liked, and stop there.

rising.upright:
With the Sun ruling your chart, Leo rising walks in and the room notices. You're warm, a bit theatrical, and people tend to decide they like you before you've said much. The Page of Swords changes what they notice. Instead of the warmth first, they get the wit, a quick line, a sharp observation, a question that makes someone laugh and then think. Air and fire are good friends, so this sits naturally, and it makes you very good company.

Look at how the figure stands in the Rider-Waite card, up on a ridge with the wind in the clouds and the sword raised, clearly enjoying being up there. That's roughly the look you're giving off. It's confident. It can also be a little cheeky, and Leo rising sometimes forgets that not everyone wants to be the straight man in your routine. Fixed fire likes to keep the spotlight once it's got it. The Page is young enough to want to be clever first and kind second, and you'll need to watch for that in yourself.

It's excellent for presentations, interviews, speeches, anything where you need to hold a room and think on your feet. Socially it makes you the one people want at the table. Let someone else get the last good line at least once in an evening.
rising.reversed:
Leo rising with the Page reversed can show off. You correct people in front of others, top every story, and make jokes that get a laugh and cost you a friend. With the Sun ruling your chart, being seen matters a great deal to you, and the upside-down card turns that into scoring points. Sometimes it's the opposite, a sudden shyness covered with sarcasm.

You'll see it at parties and in meetings, especially with anyone you think is competing with you. Online it can be the clever reply you regret by morning. People usually forgive Leo rising a lot, and they notice when you keep testing it. Next time you've got the perfect put-down ready, ask the person a question instead and see what you learn.

sun.upright:
The Page of Swords reads the instructions, and so does a Virgo Sun. Virgo is mutable earth, ruled by Mercury, and you want to be good at something real, useful, measurably improved by your being there. Mercury is the planet of the mind, so you've got a natural sympathy with this airy card that the other earth signs lack. The elements still pull apart, though. Air is ideas, earth is results, and for you the friction usually sits right there.

You're probably learning something, or investigating something, and enjoying it. The trouble starts when the research gets more interesting than the thing it was for. The Hermit is Virgo's Major, the lone figure on a mountain with a lantern, and Virgo has a real gift for that sort of patient private study. The Page is younger and more restless, wanting to know everything at once, and that combination can leave you with fourteen pages of notes and nothing yet done. You know the difference between knowing about a thing and being able to do it, and you've been sitting on the knowing side for a while.

At work it could be a new system you're learning inside out. With your health, it might be looking into how you eat or sleep. Take one thing you've found out and use it, on an ordinary day, and see what happens.
sun.reversed:
With a Virgo Sun, the reversed Page often shows up as criticism with nowhere useful to go. You spot every mistake in a colleague's report and say so, or you pick apart your own work until you can't bear to hand it in. Mercury rules Virgo, and upside down the quick mind turns fussy and sharp, correcting when nobody asked.

It can also be research as a way of never starting, reading one more review before you book, one more article before you change anything. Work shows it most, and your own health habits, where you know exactly what you should do and haven't done it. Hand in the next thing at the point where it's good enough. Leave the last round of edits undone and see whether anyone notices.

moon.upright:
A tidy kitchen settles a Virgo Moon, and so does a plan with the steps written down. Your Moon is in mutable earth, ruled by Mercury, and you feel safe when things are in order and you know what's happening next. The Page of Swords brings a lot of new information into that, and air and earth work against each other. Your body wants the routine. Your head keeps getting handed new things to think about.

It can feel like an overfull inbox. You're noticing more, picking up on small shifts in people's moods, catching details at work others miss, and every one of them wants filing. Virgo Moons tend to deal with feelings by doing something useful, and that's fine up to a point. What the Page asks is that you notice which of these thoughts are real concerns and which are just noise. That's a skill you already have for other people's problems. You're usually less good at it for your own.

Your daily routine is where it'll show, in whether you're eating properly and getting outside. Sleep is the other place, especially if you're doing your thinking in bed. Keep a notebook by the bed and write the worry down when it comes, so it's out of your head and on paper till morning.
moon.reversed:
Worry wearing a practical face is the usual shape of this for a Virgo Moon. You're not anxious, you're just checking the locks again, rereading the email before you send it, looking up a symptom at eleven at night. The Page reversed is a mind that won't settle, and in a mutable earth Moon ruled by Mercury it tends to settle on small, fixable things so it doesn't have to face the bigger feeling underneath.

It shows in routines that have tightened, in sleep, and in being short with whoever you live with about how the dishwasher's loaded. Choose a time each evening after which you don't check anything. Leave the laptop shut after eight and do something with your hands until bed.

rising.upright:
Virgo rising misses nothing. Strangers notice you're neat, polite, a little reserved, and quietly taking everything in, and with Mercury ruling your chart your first move in any situation is to observe. The Page is an observer too, with its head turned to catch what's going on. The difference is that it says what it sees. Air and earth are at odds, so the card doesn't sit quietly under your composure, and people get a sharper, more outspoken version of you.

You might find yourself pointing out the flaw in a plan at the first meeting, or asking the question that shows you've read the fine print. People will see you as clever, precise and a bit formidable. Some will be glad of it, since you're saving them trouble. Others may feel checked over, as if you're marking their work. Mutable earth adapts well, and you'll pick up quickly on which people like the directness and which don't.

It's good for a new job, especially in anything technical, or where quality matters. It's less good for a first date, where precision can come across as judgement. Say something you like about a person or a place before you say what could be better, and notice how much further the second comment goes.
rising.reversed:
Virgo rising with the Page reversed can come across as a critic. You correct someone's grammar, point out the typo in the menu, mention the better way to do it before anyone asked. It's usually nerves, the Mercury side of your chart trying to feel in control of an unfamiliar room, and people only see the red pen.

It shows at work, especially with new colleagues, and in any setting where you're being assessed and decide to assess first. It can also go inward, so you seem stiff and careful and hardly say anything in case it's wrong. The quiet version gets read as disapproval, which is rarely what it is. Next time you notice a mistake that doesn't matter, let it go past. Ask someone about their work, and just listen.

sun.upright:
Libra and this Page share an element and a lot of habits. Your Sun is in cardinal air, ruled by Venus, and Libra is one of the three signs the card is drawn from, so there's no friction of element here at all. Both of you like to weigh things up, both of you like a good conversation, and both of you notice when something's unfair. The card turns that up. For a Libra Sun that usually means the fairness gets sharper and the tact gets thinner.

You want to be liked, and that's no weakness in a Libra. It's how you build a life, through relationships that work and rooms that feel right. What the Page brings is the urge to ask the question that might upset the balance, the one about money in a relationship, or why a friend always cancels, or who actually did the work on the project. Justice is Libra's Major, and in that card the sword is held upright next to the scales. The Page has only picked up the sword so far. You're being asked to use it, gently, and to find out that a fair question doesn't make you unkind.

In a partnership it could be the conversation about how things are split. At work, it might be the meeting where you say the plan doesn't add up. Ask it in a calm voice, and then let the pause after it go on.
sun.reversed:
A Libra Sun with this card reversed tends to say the fair-sounding thing and mean something sharper. You're sweet to someone's face and quietly cutting about them later. Or you weigh a decision for so long, collecting everyone's view, that the chance goes past. Venus rules Libra and it hates a scene, which is how this gets going. Doubled air, turned over, has lots of words and very little backbone.

It shows in relationships, where you agree in the moment and resent it later, and in groups at work, where you tell each side they're right. People tend to find out. Pick one opinion you've been hedging and say it once, to the person it concerns. Let them disagree with you, and don't take it back.

moon.upright:
Arguments unsettle a Libra Moon more than almost anything. You need the people around you to be getting on, and you'll work quite hard behind the scenes to make that happen. Your Moon is in cardinal air, ruled by Venus, and the Page of Swords comes from air too, one of the family, so it speaks the way your feelings already speak. That's comfortable, and it also means the card turns everything up.

What you'll likely notice is a lot of weighing. Every feeling comes with a counter-feeling, every choice with a list of pros and cons. You can see everyone's side, which is a lovely quality, and it can leave you not knowing what you want yourself. The Page adds honesty to that. It's a card that wants to say the true thing, and a Libra Moon often knows the true thing and holds it back to keep the peace. There can be a feeling of words piling up behind your teeth.

With a partner, it's the small preference you've been swallowing, the restaurant, the weekend plans, the way they talk to you when they're tired. With friends it's being asked to take sides. Say one true preference out loud, about something small, and let the other person adjust to it.
moon.reversed:
Reversed on a Libra Moon, the Page tends to turn weighing into dithering. You can't decide, so you ask everyone, and every opinion unsettles you further. Or the feelings you've held back come out sideways, a polite little dig, a remark about someone to a third person that you'd never make to their face. Cardinal air likes to act, and when it can't act on the feeling it acts on the talk instead.

Relationships are where it shows, and group chats, where it's easy to vent to one friend about another. Sleep can go too, with conversations replaying. Make one decision you've been stalling on, on your own, without polling anyone. Then tell the person you've been talking about what you actually think, kindly and directly.

rising.upright:
First impressions are something Libra rising does well. Venus is your chart ruler, and you tend to arrive pleasant, polished and easy to be around, the person who makes a stranger feel at ease. This Page is air, like your rising sign, and belongs to the same airy group, so it slots in easily. What it adds is an edge to the charm. You're still lovely to meet. You're also asking better questions and saying what you think sooner.

People might find you more interesting and a little less predictable. There's a directness under the good manners that shows up in the first conversation, a frank opinion, a question someone wasn't expecting from you. Cardinal air starts things through other people, and the Page gives you the nerve to start with honesty. It can feel risky, because part of Libra rising's ease comes from never quite showing where it stands. Here it shows. Most people will like you better for it, though one or two who liked the smooth version may be thrown.

This is useful in negotiation, interviews, dating, anywhere charm alone wouldn't get you far enough. It's good for any work where you represent other people. When someone asks your opinion, give it first and soften it second, if at all.
rising.reversed:
With Libra rising and the Page reversed, the charm can start to feel slippery. You agree with everyone in the room, then say something quite pointed once they've gone. Or the manners stay perfect and the remarks underneath get sharper, a compliment with a sting in the tail. Venus rules your chart, and in this reversal it keeps the surface smooth and lets the air come out as barbs.

People pick up on it at work and in social groups, where you're liked but never quite trusted. On dates it can look like flirting that's mostly teasing. Libra rising can be very funny, and this is the one place it costs you. Next time you're about to make a light, cutting joke about someone, drop it. Say the plain, kind version, or say nothing.

sun.upright:
Scorpio has always been the investigator of the zodiac, and the Page of Swords is the youngest investigator in the deck. Scorpio is fixed water, ruled by Mars and by Pluto in the modern scheme, and a Scorpio Sun wants to get to the bottom of things and hold on to what it finds. The card belongs to air, and water and air have no particular bond. They need introducing. Where you go in quietly and deep, the Page goes in asking out loud.

That's the tension, and it's a real one. You're used to finding things out without anyone knowing you're looking. This card says ask. Ask the person directly, put the question on the table, find out in daylight. For a Scorpio Sun that can feel like handing over power, since knowing and keeping quiet has always been part of how you protect yourself. Death is Scorpio's Major, the card of things ending so something else can start, and the Page often arrives when an old way of keeping secrets is ready to finish. You may be surprised how much lighter it feels to just know.

With money, it might be a joint account or a debt you've been quietly worrying about. In a relationship, it's the question you've been circling for months. Ask it in plain words and let the answer be what it is.
sun.reversed:
Scorpio's intensity and the Page's sharp tongue can make a nasty mix, and with a Scorpio Sun and this card reversed you may be using what you know as a weapon. You've found something out, and you're holding it, waiting for the right moment. Or you're snooping, reading a message over someone's shoulder, piecing together a story you haven't been told. Fixed water keeps things, and the upside-down air card keeps them sharp.

It shows in close relationships and at work, especially around rivals. Sometimes it's words said to wound in an argument, the precise ones that go straight to a weak spot. Scorpio always knows where that spot is. Say what you know, or let it go, and stop keeping it in reserve.

moon.upright:
Trust is what a Scorpio Moon needs, and it doesn't hand it out easily. You feel things all the way down, you keep most of it to yourself, and you'd honestly prefer to know the worst than be kept in the dark. Your Moon is in fixed water. This card is air, which neither helps nor hinders water on its own, so the two have to find a way to work together.

The Page is watchful, and a Scorpio Moon is watchful, so the first thing you might notice is how closely you're paying attention to people. You catch the pause before an answer, the change in someone's tone, the story that doesn't quite add up. Sometimes you're right. Sometimes you're reading your own fear into it. The card's gift is that it asks questions out loud, and for a Scorpio Moon that's the healthier route. Suspicion that stays in your head grows. Asked plainly, it usually shrinks back down to its real size.

Intimacy is where this lives, with a partner especially, where you want to know where you stand. It shows at night too, in thoughts that get darker after midnight. When you notice you're building a case against someone, stop and ask them the one question the case depends on.
moon.reversed:
A reversed Page on a Scorpio Moon can turn watchfulness into surveillance. You're checking who liked what, reading between every line, keeping a quiet record of slights. Fixed water holds on to feelings, and this card upside down gives them a suspicious mind to live in, one that assumes the worst and then looks for proof. Sometimes the suspicion's aimed at yourself, a running commentary on everything you did wrong.

It shows in relationships, in the phone you check and the questions you ask in a certain tone, and in sleep that goes light and restless. It costs the people around you, who feel watched. Pick the suspicion that's loudest, say it to the person calmly, and accept the answer you're given for at least a week.

rising.upright:
Scorpio rising gives people a look they remember. You're self-contained, intense, and hard to read, and strangers can feel they've been seen through in the first few minutes. Mars rules Scorpio, with Pluto as its modern ruler, so your chart ruler gives your first moves a guarded strength. The Page of Swords adds a question to that stare. Air and water have to be introduced to each other, and this card makes the introduction by putting words where there was usually silence.

People might notice you're talking more, and what you say is pointed. You ask the direct question that someone else would tiptoe around. You say out loud what the whole meeting is thinking. That can be startling from Scorpio rising, who usually keeps its observations to itself, and people who thought they had you worked out may be surprised. There's a kind of relief in it. You don't have to carry every observation silently any more.

It's very useful anywhere you need to get to the truth quickly, research, negotiation, a difficult conversation with a landlord or a boss. On a first date it'll make you intriguing, though it may feel like an interview to the other person. Tell them something about yourself in return for each thing you ask.
rising.reversed:
Scorpio rising with this Page reversed can feel like an interrogation to the people you meet. You ask too much, give nothing back, and leave them feeling exposed. Or the mask goes cold and cutting, a dry remark that lands exactly where it hurts. Mars runs your chart, and the reversed card turns that edge into words. Most of the time you're protecting yourself, and nobody can see that from the outside.

You'll see it in new workplaces where people are wary of you after one meeting, and on dates that feel like a cross-examination. It can also show as secrecy, refusing to answer simple questions about yourself. Offer one piece of personal information early in each new meeting. It gives people something to hold on to, and they'll relax around you.

sun.upright:
There's a lot of sky in the Rider-Waite picture for this card, wind pushing the clouds along and birds scattered high up, and a Sagittarius Sun would feel at home under it. Sagittarius is mutable fire, ruled by Jupiter, and you want to go further, learn more and find out what it all means. The Page is air, which feeds fire, so this is an easy, lively pairing. Your curiosity gets a sharper edge and your honesty gets quicker.

What it feels like is appetite. You want to read the book, take the course, argue about the big question over a long dinner. You're asking why, and you won't settle for a comforting answer. Temperance belongs to Sagittarius among the Majors, and that card is all patience, pouring the same water back and forth until it's right. That's the part the Page hasn't got yet. Mutable fire can start a dozen subjects and drop them when the excitement fades, and a Page who keeps changing subjects stays a Page. Most Sagittarius Suns I've seen get their real depth from the one subject they didn't drop.

Study is the obvious place, a qualification, a language, something you've always meant to learn properly. Travel is another, especially a trip where you're asking locals questions and getting lost on purpose. With friends, it's the big late-night argument you both enjoy. Choose one subject and give it a proper term, with a start date and an end date written down.
sun.reversed:
Reversed with a Sagittarius Sun, the Page can turn into a know-it-all. You've read one article and you're lecturing the table. You're blunt with someone who needed gentleness, and you call it honesty. Jupiter rules Sagittarius and makes things bigger, including opinions that haven't been checked. It can also look like restless learning that never lands, five courses started and none finished.

Family dinners and group chats bring it out, and so does any conversation about politics or belief. Friends might have started changing the subject when you get going. It isn't malice. You get excited and forget to look at faces. Before you share the next strong opinion, find out one thing about where the other person's coming from, and then decide whether it still needs saying.

moon.upright:
A Sagittarius Moon needs room. Space to move, something to look forward to, the sense that tomorrow could be different. Your Moon is in mutable fire, ruled by Jupiter, and you tend to cheer yourself up by planning, learning, or getting out of the house. The Page is an air card, and air and fire get along very well, so your feelings run quick and bright, full of ideas.

It can feel like mental wanderlust. You're curious about everything, making plans at midnight, reading about places you might go and things you might do. That's lovely, and it's also how a Sag Moon avoids sitting still with a feeling. The Page is restless by nature, and together you can go a long time without noticing you're a bit lonely, or tired, or worried about someone. The honesty in this card helps, though. When you do stop and ask yourself what's going on, you'll get a straight answer, and Sagittarius Moons usually take the truth well.

In your body it shows as a need to move, walk, get outside. At home it can look like the itch to be somewhere else, which a partner might take personally. Go on the long walk, leave the podcast off, and let whatever you're feeling catch up with you on the way back.
moon.reversed:
When a Sagittarius Moon draws this card reversed, the restless mind can run away with the feelings. You're anxious and don't know why, so you plan a trip, sign up for something, start three conversations at once. Mutable fire can always find a new direction, and the reversed Page scatters it further. Jupiter rules your Moon's sign, and it makes everything larger, including the worry.

Sometimes it's bluntness at the wrong moment, a joke or a truth delivered when someone needed comfort. It shows at home and in friendships, and in sleep that's broken by a busy head. Stay in for an evening you'd normally fill. Cook something slow, leave the phone in another room, and notice what feeling turns up when there's nothing to plan.

rising.upright:
Frank, friendly and a bit loud is the usual first impression of Sagittarius rising. Jupiter rules your chart, and you tend to meet people with enthusiasm and a joke, as if the next conversation might be an adventure. The Page of Swords gives that openness a sharper point. Fire and air suit each other, so this sits well, and people meet someone curious, quick and startlingly direct.

You ask strangers big questions, what they believe, why they moved, what they'd do if they could do anything. People tend to love it or feel slightly put on the spot. You'll also say what you think very early, and Sagittarius rising is already known for that, so it can be a lot. The Page's honesty is young and doesn't always check who's listening. Mutable fire moves fast, and you'll probably have moved on before you notice someone was stung.

It's great for travel, teaching, interviews and any new group where people need livening up. On a date, you'll be memorable. Keep an eye on faces as you talk, and if someone goes quiet after one of your remarks, go back and ask about it.
rising.reversed:
Sagittarius rising and a reversed Page can make for foot-in-mouth days. You say the tactless thing in the first minute, or you make a joke about someone's job, religion or hometown and watch it land badly. With Jupiter ruling your chart, you're used to being forgiven for bluntness, and this upside-down card tests that. Most of it's enthusiasm, and people can't always tell.

It can also look like overpromising, telling a new contact you'll introduce them to everyone and then forgetting. It shows at work events, weddings, anywhere with mixed company. Online it's the hot take posted from the airport. When you meet someone new, let them talk for the first few minutes. Save your opinion until you know a little about who you're giving it to.

sun.upright:
Capricorn respects an apprenticeship, and this Page is an apprentice. Your Sun is in cardinal earth, ruled by Saturn, and you build yourself through effort, competence and results you can point to. The Page is air, and air and earth are opposed, one full of questions and the other wanting proof. That friction is real for a Capricorn Sun, and it's also useful.

You may find you're being asked to learn something new at a stage when you'd rather be the expert. A new role, a new system, a field where you're junior again. It can sting. Saturn likes to have earned its place, and being the beginner feels like losing ground. The Devil is Capricorn's Major, the card of what keeps us chained, and for Capricorn one of those chains is being unable to look inexperienced. The Page doesn't mind asking a basic question in a room full of seniors. It asks, writes the answer down, and gets on with it.

At work it's the course, the certification, the mentor you'd benefit from. In your family, it could be a younger relative who knows something you don't, a teenager explaining the new phone, perhaps. Ask the basic question out loud in front of someone senior, and then ask the follow-up.
sun.reversed:
A reversed Page with a Capricorn Sun often turns into cynicism. Someone brings you a new idea and you've listed its flaws before they've finished explaining. You've seen it all before, you think, and some of the time you have. Saturn rules Capricorn, and upside down the questioning mind hardens into dismissal, the old hand sneering at the new kid.

It can also look like refusing to learn a thing because you'd have to admit you don't know it. Work is the usual place, with younger colleagues especially, and family too. The people who bring you ideas start bringing them to someone else. Next time someone junior suggests something, ask them two questions about it before you give your view.

moon.upright:
Being in control soothes a Capricorn Moon. You feel safest when you're competent, when there's a plan, when you've got the responsible version of things in hand. Your Moon is in cardinal earth, ruled by Saturn, which gives your feelings a sturdy structure. The Page brings air into that, and earth and air are opposed, so the feeling is a bit like wind getting under a roof. Things that were nailed down start to rattle.

Mostly it comes as thinking. Worries about work, what-ifs about money, rehearsing a difficult conversation in the shower. A Capricorn Moon deals with anxiety by planning, and the Page gives you plenty of material to plan with. Some of that is useful. The rest is your mind trying to control something that can't be controlled yet. The honest side of this card might also bring up a question you've been avoiding about your own needs, like whether you're doing all this because you want to or because you feel you should.

Sleep is usually the first thing to go, early waking with your head already at work. With family, it's being the one who sorts everything and noticing, for once, that you'd like someone else to. Write the worry list down in the evening, close the notebook, and leave the solving for daylight.
moon.reversed:
With a Capricorn Moon, a reversed Page often means worry disguised as planning. You'd say you're just thinking ahead, three contingencies deep, at two in the morning. Saturn rules the sign your Moon is in, and with the card upside down its caution gets a restless, nagging voice that won't let anything rest. Capricorn Moons carry a lot quietly, and that's exactly the problem here.

It can also come out as a dry, cutting remark to someone who didn't deserve it, because you're tired and nobody noticed. The people close to you often can't tell anything's wrong until you snap. Work and home both carry it. Tell one person you're worried, in plain words, without offering the plan alongside. Let them just hear it.

rising.upright:
Capricorn rising usually walks in looking like the most sensible person in the room. Saturn rules your chart, and you come across as composed, capable and a bit reserved, someone who won't waste words. The Page of Swords sharpens that composure into something more pointed. Air and earth don't naturally agree, so the card doesn't blend in, and people notice a questioning, slightly exacting edge.

You ask the question that shows you've done your homework, and possibly that they haven't. You're quicker to challenge a claim, and people see you as clever, serious and perhaps a bit intimidating. Cardinal earth likes to start things with a plan, and the Page gives you the urge to test the plan out loud first. Some colleagues will appreciate it, since you're catching problems early. Others might feel you're checking up on them. You can come across as older than you are anyway, and this adds to it, unless you let the Page's youthful curiosity show as well.

In interviews and meetings, this makes you look very competent. In social settings, it can make people nervous. Try asking one question purely out of interest, something with no agenda behind it, and let people see you enjoy the answer.
rising.reversed:
Capricorn rising can come across as curt when the Page is reversed. You answer in as few words as possible, pick holes in what someone's proposing, and look faintly unimpressed. It's often shyness or strain behind the Saturn-ruled front, and people read it as disapproval and back away. Saturn can make a person look older and sterner than they feel, and this doubles it.

It shows in first meetings, particularly at work, and anywhere you feel judged and decide to judge first. Sometimes it's the reverse, a nervous chatter that isn't like you at all. Make a point of being warm in the first thirty seconds with someone new. A smile and a proper hello will do a lot of the work for you.

sun.upright:
An Aquarius Sun wants to think for itself, and the Page of Swords is the youngest free thinker in the deck. Aquarius is fixed air, ruled by Saturn with Uranus as its modern ruler, and it's one of the air signs this court card is built from. So the card speaks your language, and it amplifies you, the independence, the originality, the habit of questioning the way things are done. It amplifies the stubbornness too.

Fixed air holds on to its ideas once it has them, and the Page is all fresh questions, which gives you an interesting push and pull. You might be rethinking something you've been sure of for years, an opinion about a group you belong to or a cause you've backed. The Star is Aquarius's Major, the card of hope and of looking a long way ahead, and the Page is the part of you that's still asking what's true on the way there. You may enjoy being the awkward one in a room, the person who asks why the rule exists. Be honest with yourself about whether you're asking because you want to know or because you like being contrary.

In groups and friendships, this could mean a proper debate that changes someone's mind, possibly yours. In your work, it's the research or technical problem you can't leave alone. Pick one belief you hold firmly and read the best argument against it, all the way through.
sun.reversed:
Contrarian for the sake of it is the usual trouble with a reversed Page on an Aquarius Sun. You argue with everything, pick the opposite side on principle, and enjoy the argument more than the answer. Doubled air, turned over, can get very clever and very cold. Fixed air also means you'll dig in once you've started, even when you half suspect you're wrong. Saturn rules Aquarius, and upside down it can make you rigid about being unconventional.

It shows online, in group chats, in the committee meeting where you've become the person everyone sighs at. Sometimes it's quieter, a detached, superior silence while others talk. Friends may be tired of it. Next time you disagree, say what you agree with first, and then decide whether the rest is worth a fight.

moon.upright:
Aquarius Moons like a bit of distance from their feelings. You need space, independence, friends who don't crowd you, and you tend to understand an emotion by thinking about it from a step back. Your Moon is in fixed air, ruled by Saturn and by Uranus in the modern view, and this card belongs to the same element and the same airy family. So nothing here pushes back. It's air on air, and that's comfortable and a bit much at once.

What you might notice is that your mind's very busy and your feelings are hard to reach. You're interested in everything, reading, debating, thinking about big problems, and underneath there's something quieter you haven't looked at. The Page is honest, though, and if you point it at yourself it'll give you a clear answer. Aquarius Moons are often better at naming their feelings than people assume. You just like to do it in your own time and in private.

Friendships are where this shows most, especially the ones where you talk about ideas for hours and never about yourselves. Sleep can go light when your head's busy. Tell one friend something true about how you are, and let the conversation stay there for a while.
moon.reversed:
Reversed on an Aquarius Moon, this Page can freeze the feelings out altogether. You explain your mood as if it belonged to someone else, give a clever analysis of why you're upset, and never quite feel it. Or you swamp yourself with information, news, forums, documentaries, anything to keep the mind busy and the feeling at arm's length. Fixed air can keep this up for a surprisingly long time.

It shows in friendships that have gone a bit cool, and in sleep, which gets light and restless. People close to you may feel they can't reach you, and they may have stopped trying. Turn off the feed for an evening. Spend it with one person you trust, and talk about something that isn't an idea.

rising.upright:
Aquarius rising tends to strike people as friendly but slightly hard to place. You're open, a little unusual, interested in ideas, and there's a cool, independent air to how you meet the world. Saturn rules your chart, with Uranus as the modern co-ruler, and fixed air gives you a steady way of being yourself in any room. The Page is air too, from the same airy family, so it doesn't change you so much as sharpen you.

People will notice the questions. You're asking things that make them think, challenging an assumption in the first conversation, taking the unexpected side just to see what happens. You'll come across as clever, original, and a bit provocative. Some people will love the challenge. Others will find it unsettling that you won't do the usual small talk. There's a youthful quality too, the look of someone who's still curious, whatever your age.

It's a great card for group work, for anything to do with technology or new ideas, and for meeting people online, where your wit comes through. On first dates it can make you memorable and a bit mysterious. Once in a while, answer a question about yourself before you ask one back.
rising.reversed:
An Aquarius rising with the Page reversed can seem aloof or deliberately difficult. You play devil's advocate in the first five minutes, or you stand at the edge of the party making dry observations to one person. With Saturn ruling your chart, the reversed card turns independence into distance, and people decide you're not interested in them. Fixed air holds a pose well, and this one's harder to drop than it should be.

It shows in groups, at work, and online, where provoking people is easy and costs more than you think. Sometimes it's shyness that looks like superiority. Find one person at the next gathering and ask them about something they care about. Then stay in that conversation longer than feels natural.

sun.upright:
A sword is about the last thing a Pisces Sun expects to be handed. Pisces is mutable water, ruled by Jupiter and in modern astrology by Neptune, and you tend to live by feeling and imagination, soaking up the moods around you. Swords are the air suit, and water and air have no natural pull toward or away from each other, so they need an introduction. What the Page brings you is clarity, and clarity isn't always a Pisces favourite.

It can feel like someone opening the curtains in a room you were quite happy to keep dim. There's a fact you've been avoiding, or a person you've been seeing through a soft focus, and suddenly the edges are sharp. The Moon is Pisces's Major, a card about not being sure what's real, and the Page is its opposite, a young mind determined to find out. For a Pisces Sun that's uncomfortable, and also a relief. Mutable water takes the shape of whatever holds it, and you've been taking the shape of someone else's story for a while.

In creative work this is an editor's card, cutting what doesn't work, getting the idea down clearly. In relationships, it's seeing a partner or friend as they really are, without the story you've added. Write the thing you've been vague about in one plain sentence, and read it back to yourself.
sun.reversed:
A Pisces Sun with this Page reversed may be believing whatever it's told. A rumour lands and you absorb it, a friend's version of events becomes yours, and you don't ask the obvious question. Mutable water takes on everything around it, and the reversed air card muddles it further. Sometimes it goes the other way and you're uncharacteristically sharp, snapping at someone because you're overwhelmed.

It shows at work, in gossip you get pulled into, and in relationships, where you've avoided a clear conversation for months. Jupiter and Neptune both widen things, and neither of them is much help with facts. Check one thing you've taken on trust. Ask the source directly, and keep the conversation short and plain.

moon.upright:
Pisces Moons soak up everything, the mood of the room, the news, the friend's sad story, the song on the radio. You need quiet and gentleness, and time alone to wring yourself out. Your Moon is in mutable water, ruled by Jupiter with Neptune as its modern ruler. This is an air card, and water doesn't naturally know how to talk to air, so it brings a sharpness your Moon isn't used to.

It might feel like being more alert than you'd like. You notice when someone's lying. You catch the tone in a message. You're less willing to believe the kind version of a story, and that can be unsettling for a Moon that usually gives everyone the benefit of the doubt. There's also a lot of mental noise, the worry about what someone meant, the imagined conversation, and a Pisces Moon's imagination can make any of it vivid. The good side is protection. A sword can draw a line, and you may find you're better at saying no than usual.

Sleep is where it shows, especially vivid dreams or waking to a racing mind. With friends, it's the one who leans on you too much. Say no to one thing you'd normally agree to out of kindness, and give a short, clear reason.
moon.reversed:
With a Pisces Moon, the Page reversed can turn imagination into anxiety. A vague message becomes a disaster in your head. You hear half a story and fill in the rest, usually the worst version. Mutable water has no firm edges, and a restless, reversed air card blows all sorts of fears across it.

It can also show as avoidance, letters left unopened, messages left unanswered, hoping the problem goes vague and drifts off. Pisces Moons are brave about other people's troubles and easily frightened by their own post. Sleep suffers, and so does your patience with busy people. Pick the one thing you've been imagining the worst about and find out the facts. Most of the time the real version is smaller.

rising.upright:
Soft and dreamy is how people usually first read Pisces rising. You come across gentle, a bit elusive, easy to confide in, and strangers can feel you're somehow already on their side. Jupiter rules your chart, with Neptune as its modern ruler, and it gives your approach to the world a wide, open quality. The Page of Swords puts a sharper look on that face. Air and water are strangers to each other, so it's an unexpected combination, and people may be surprised.

They'll see someone who's paying close attention, who asks a pointed question when they expected sympathy, who seems to know when they're being fed a line. That can be very good for you. Pisces rising sometimes gets taken advantage of because it seems so accommodating, and the Page makes you look like someone who'll check. You might feel it too, a clearer, quicker way of starting things. Mutable water usually waits to see how a situation's going before it moves, and this time you're moving first.

At work it helps with negotiation and anything where you need to be taken seriously. In dating it can stop you drifting into something you're not sure about. Ask one practical question early, about plans, money or intentions, and listen closely to the answer.
rising.reversed:
Pisces rising with this Page reversed can seem evasive. You give vague answers, change the subject when a question gets direct, and people aren't sure what you actually think. Sometimes it's a sudden sharp remark from someone they'd assumed was gentle, and it throws them. The reversed card muddles your usual softness with nerves, and it comes out either foggy or prickly.

You'll see it in new jobs, early dating and family gatherings, anywhere you feel on show. People who'd like to trust you can't find much to hold on to. Choose a simple, honest answer to the question you get asked most, what you do, how you are, what you want, and practise saying it. Then use it the next time someone asks.

1.upright:
The first house is the front door of the chart, how you carry yourself, how you start things, the body you walk around in. It's angular, one of the four corners, so whatever lands here gets seen. By nature it's Aries territory, ruled by Mars, and fire and air feed each other, which means the Page's quick mind turns into action here almost without a gap. There's also an old tradition that Mercury, the planet of words and wits, has its joy in the first house. The Page has no planet of its own, but it's all wits and words, so it's very much at home.

What that looks like is a sharper, more alert version of you. You're noticing more, asking more, and deciding things faster. You might change something about how you present yourself, a haircut, a new way of speaking up in meetings, and it'll be because you've thought about it, not because you drifted into it. The risk is starting several things on the strength of one bright idea each. The first house is about beginnings, and the Page loves a beginning. Finishing is somebody else's department as far as this card's concerned.

In the body, this is a restless, get-up-and-go energy that wants movement, a new sport, a walk with a podcast, anything that keeps the mind busy. At work, it's the fresh start where you're the one asking the questions. Choose one new thing to begin, and tell someone you'll report back on how it went.
1.reversed:
In the first house a reversed Page can make you jumpy. You start things and drop them, speak before you've thought, and come across as edgier than you mean to. The body picks it up too, as a wired, tense feeling, shallow breathing, fidgeting in meetings. Mars rules this house by nature, and with the card upside down the air stirs up irritation more easily than curiosity.

It shows in how you meet people, in the quick defensive answer, and in a string of fresh starts that never quite get going. Pick one of the things you've started and see it through to a small finish. Then do something physical every day, even briefly, to give the restlessness somewhere to go.

2.upright:
Actual money is the second house's business, the bank balance, the pay, the things you own, and alongside it the quieter question of what you think you're worth. It's a succedent house, the kind that builds up and holds on. Taurus is its natural sign and Venus its natural ruler, and earth and air sit on opposite sides, idea against matter. So the Page of Swords brings questions into a house that would much prefer certainty.

Usually that's a good thing. The Page reads the fine print. It wants to know where the money's going, what the fees are, why the pay rise hasn't come. You may find you're finally looking at the statements you've been avoiding, or researching a better account, or working out what your time is actually worth per hour. The friction is that learning about money and changing what you do with it are two different skills. The second house wants to see something solid at the end, and the Page can get so interested in the research that it forgets to move the money.

It also touches self-worth. You might be asking whether you're being paid fairly, or whether you've undersold yourself somewhere, in a job or a quote or a salary conversation. Look at one account or one bill properly, line by line, and make one change based on what you find.
2.reversed:
Money anxiety is often what a reversed Page stirs up in the second house. You check the balance three times a day, read every scary article about the economy, or lie awake doing sums. The other version is carelessness, buying on impulse, trusting a tip from someone who sounded confident, signing without reading. Earth and air pull against each other, and upside down the pull turns into nerves or recklessness.

Self-worth can wobble too, especially if someone's made a sharp comment about what you earn or own. Venus is this house's natural ruler, and it likes to feel secure before it can enjoy anything. Make a simple list, what comes in, what goes out, and what you've got. Look at it once, on a set day, and leave it alone between times.

3.upright:
This is the Page's home ground. The third house covers words, messages, siblings, neighbours, short trips and everyday learning, and its natural sign is Gemini, ruled by Mercury. Gemini is one of the air signs the Page is drawn from, so card and house speak the same language and the card gets louder here, in both directions.

Expect lots of talk. Messages, calls, emails, conversations with a brother or sister, the neighbour who stops you at the gate. You'll want to learn something, a short course, a language app, a new skill you can pick up quickly. The third house is cadent, the kind of house that processes and adjusts, and that's what the Page is doing, taking in information and sorting it. The Moon has its joy here in the old tradition, which is a fair hint that everyday talk carries feeling too. A sharp word to a sibling lands harder than you'd think.

Short journeys are part of this, the commute, the drive to see family, the walk to the shops, and they're where a lot of the thinking gets done. With siblings or cousins, an honest conversation could clear something old. Keep a notebook for the ideas that come on the move, and read back through it every so often to see which ones are still worth anything.
3.reversed:
The third house is where a reversed Page does its gossiping. Something told in confidence gets passed on. A message gets forwarded that shouldn't have been. You misread a text from a sibling and reply sharply, and now there's a whole thing. Air in air, upside down, makes lots of chatter and little clarity, and the scattered attention shows up as missed messages and half-finished courses.

It's worth being careful with neighbours, family group chats and anything you put in writing. Short trips can be a bit chaotic too, wrong turns, forgotten keys. Mercury rules this house by nature, and a reversed Page gives Mercury's worst habits free rein. Before you send anything with an edge, read it back out loud. If it sounds worse spoken, don't send it.

4.upright:
Home and family sit in the fourth house, the private ground at the bottom of the chart, where you come from and where you go to recover. It's angular, so what happens here matters, even if nobody outside sees it. Cancer is the sign that naturally belongs here, with the Moon as ruler. Air and water don't quarrel and don't naturally understand each other either, so the Page's clear, questioning mind has to find a way into a house that runs on feeling.

Very often that means questions about family. Where a grandparent came from. Why there's a rift between two relatives nobody talks about. What the real arrangement is with the house, the lease, a parent's care. You might find yourself doing family history, or having a conversation over dinner where someone finally says what happened. That can be uncomfortable, since the fourth house is where old habits and old silences live. The Page isn't cruel about it. It just wants to know, and it's young enough to ask.

In your own home, it can mean a clear-out driven by practical thinking, labelling, sorting, making the place work better. With the people you live with, it might be a proper talk about how the household's run. Ask one family question you've always wondered about, of the person most likely to know.
4.reversed:
Sharp words find their way into the home with this card reversed in the fourth house. Arguments at dinner, sarcastic remarks between people who love each other, a sibling who repeats something that should've stayed private. Or the family keeps things from each other, and you can feel the gaps in the stories without being able to say what's missing.

It can also be your own mind that won't settle at home, lying awake, going over old family things. Sleep is often the first thing to go, and after that your patience. The Moon is the natural ruler here, so moods travel fast. Pick one sore point at home and raise it calmly, in private, with the one person it concerns. Leave the rest of the family out of it.

5.upright:
Fun, flirting, making things and children all belong to the fifth house, and this Page brings wit to every one of them. The house's natural sign is Leo, ruled by the Sun, and fire and air get on very well, so this is a lively, playful placement. Venus takes its joy here in the old tradition, which is why romance lives in this house, and the Page's version of romance is banter.

What it feels like is quick, clever play. Puzzles, quizzes, word games, a group who make each other laugh. In love, it's the exchange of messages that goes on all evening, teasing and back-and-forth, and a date that feels like a good argument you both enjoyed. Creatively, you might be drawn to writing, stand-up, satire, anything sharp. The fifth house is succedent, a house that builds and holds, so there's also a question of whether any of this playful energy gets kept. The Page tends to start a dozen fun things, and one of them is usually worth sticking with.
